We're working through GreenBank's audit for customer data deletion guarantees and have a couple of technical clarifications we need to include in our report:

Hi — pulled details from infra and ops; summary below (technical bits first, then a suggested plain-English blurb for auditors). Also attached: a sanitized sample trace csv that follows the pattern we can provide.

Technical summary (short):
- Delete handling: an account deletion request sets a logical tombstone at the application layer immediately (metadata timestamp T0). The primary datastore marks the record as deleted and it becomes non-queryable from the app almost immediately.
- Backup lifecycle: snapshots are taken every 24 hours; incremental checkpoints occur hourly. Backups are immutable snapshots. A tombstoned record will appear in existing snapshot files until a snapshot containing the tombstone is itself swept/expired.
- Expunge waves: we run coordinated expunge waves that remove tombstoned items from active backup manifests on a rolling schedule. Typical scheduling: daily sweep + regional wave within 72 hours for cross-region consistency. So in normal operation the effective removal from all backup manifests completes within 72 hours of the tombstone being recorded, but the exact timing depends on the snapshot cadence and regional propagation windows.
- Legal holds: if a legal hold is applied before or during the expunge window, the tombstone is flagged and excluded from expunge. Holds are checked at the start of each sweep; the presence of a hold postpones removal until the hold is cleared. Holds can extend retention beyond normal expiry and will be visible in our audit manifests.

Suggested plain-English reply for auditors (two short bullets):
- When an account is deleted, the item is marked deleted in the primary system immediately. Removal from backups occurs when the next backup-expunge wave clears tombstoned items; this typically completes within 72 hours under normal operation.
- If a legal hold is present at the time of an expunge, that item is preserved in backups until the hold is removed; holds are honored automatically and recorded in our audit manifests.

Attached: backup-trace-example.csv (sanitized) — contains a sample sequence: deletion request (T0), tombstone write, snapshot id that still contains record, expunge wave entry when removed, and hold flag if relevant.

Let me know if you want tighter SLAs or an alternate wording for compliance.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Infrastructure Operations
[Attachment: backup-trace-example.csv]
